cross_item_pattern.rule: Rule 1 (design items naming a target): when the stem names the variable or object to be tested (posture, the boulders themselves, a former lake, whether water is needed, whether the caffeine effect depends on temperature), the key is the only option that manipulates or observes that named target; every distractor varies or measures something else. Rule 2 (both-agree CV items): when the stem asks what both scientists/students would agree on, strike every option that names a mechanism rivalled by another option (glacier vs water, star heat vs interior heat, one specific tissue/process); the key is the one option naming no contested mechanism. Applied without the passage, these pick the key on 8 of 8 named items (chance 25%). Caveat for the coordinator: both rules partly follow from the stem types themselves, as on the real ACT, so they read as an item-type property more than an authoring formula; but they meet the brief's three conditions.
